newsitem.title: USA: U.S. stock index futures rise more late,end higher.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stock index futures rise more late,end higher.

text.p: July 24 - U.S. stock index futures rose again late, most ended moderately to sharply higher. Sept S&P 500s drew widespread buying late as it shook off morning sales and rose, hitting buystops near 945.00 and again near 946.50, brokers said. Although some said a correction is due, others said resilience could mean more upside first. Daily volume moderate.
Brokers said technical buying also emerged and caught shorts off guard when lead-month S&Ps managed to recover above trendline support near 932.00.
Slow erosion in U.S. Treasury futures from morning highs had undercut some support in the contract earlier, although the dollar's continued strength proved impressive.

The recovery of over-the-counter stocks from their biggest early losses also helped futures pop back up, despite ideas that stocks again are technically overextended on the upside and due for a healthy downward correction.

One floor broker said if the contract broke below the 930.00 area, it could head down toward 924.50, which he said still would not satisfy the need for a downside retracement of its rally to consecutively higher all-time highs.
"It would not be enough, not nearly enough (correction)," the broker said. "But if we can get a couple days of 600 (basis points) lower...we need a couple of these days put together."
Traders noted early signs of arb sell programs and later of buy programs as the premium alternately narrowed and widened again. Fair value Thursday was 5.60 points premium.
Arb buy programs needed about 6.90 points over cash, and sell programs required about 5.10 points premium.

At settlement, September S&P 500s were up 4.60 pts at 945.85, Value Lines rose 2.00 pts to 828.00, Nikkei 225 gained 55.0 pts to 20,350.0, Midcap 400s firmed 0.20 to 309.50, Russell fell 1.05 to 410.55, and NASDAQ fell 2.25 pts 1096.25.
